anchor: At some observation time during execution, the model must match the speculative program order and resolved and committed states in the instance.
comment: 'Observation time' (also 'time snapshot', pipeline.tex:15) is the key to reading every graph figure: the flags describe one moment, so an instruction drawn 'committed' can have been speculative earlier. It is used here and in Fig. 5's caption but never defined. Without it the interleave and OTB captions read as contradictions.
proposed: An execution graph is a snapshot of the processor at one \emph{observation time}, the tick at which the transmitter transmits: its committed and resolved flags give each instruction's state at that tick, so an instruction flagged committed may still have been speculative earlier in the run.
evidence: tikz/resolutiontiming.tex:108 ('fixes only that i0 has committed by the observation time'); check_ld.py:108-111 (lc retired and marked branches unresolved at xmit_signal). Check: resolved_before_signal is reported, not gated (URGENT_TODO fixed-harness DECIDE)

anchor: i4 now merges c0's value, which is speculative only under the older branches i0 and i1, with i3's value, which stays speculative under i2.

proposed: i4 now merges c0's value, which was speculative only until the older branches i0 and i1 resolved (both commit before the observation time), with i3's value, which is still speculative under i2.

proposed: For data-flow speculation, we instrument \emph{store bypass}: a load mispredicts that it does not alias an older store whose address is still unresolved, and reads stale memory instead of the store's value~\cite{stt}. [and in Fig.~\ref{fig:pipeline} pass 3: '(branches, store bypass)']

anchor: and \emph{observation} (existing debug flags, which expose the transmitter, as described below).
comment: The Stage-3 machinery has overlapping names: hooks (control hooks, config glue, observation), directives (speculation and timing), annotation, probes (Fig. 3, discussion), knobs, harness. 'Observation' here is what Fig. 3 calls probes. 'Non-invasive' (pipeline.tex:15, Fig. 3) is also undefined, and the hooks do change prediction and timing. Define the layers once, here.
proposed: [after this sentence] We use these words throughout: the \emph{annotation} is the per-test file Stage~2 writes; a \emph{directive} is one thing it asks gem5 to do (force a prediction, hold a resolution); a \emph{hook} is the gem5 source site that carries it out; a \emph{probe} is an existing debug trace the inspector reads; the \emph{harness} is the hooks and probes together. It is \emph{non-invasive} in that it changes only prediction and timing, never the defense's protection logic.
evidence: FIGURES.md glossary (a6); tikz/pipeline_full_8pt1col.tex:230,236; sections/discussion.tex:7; sections/pipeline.tex:15,92,128

anchor: the fnc-stall on vs.\ off, the branch-annotation on vs.\ off, and the \texttt{Unsafe}-scheme baseline

proposed: [Execution Syntax] We call the youngest committed instruction \texttt{lc} (last committed) and the oldest uncommitted one \texttt{fnc} (first uncommitted); between them lies the \emph{commit boundary}.

anchor: Data-dependence edges (rf, ddi) track information flow to transmitters.
comment: First prose use of rf and ddi, with no expansion (reviewer #71A asked for exactly this; ddi = data-dependence internal is decided). Also, Background defines rf as the MCM relation from a write to a read; SimSpect's rf links any output operand to a later input operand, registers included. Say so.
proposed: Two relations track information flow: \emph{rf} (reads-from) links an output operand to a later input operand that names the same register or memory location, generalizing the MCM reads-from relation to registers; \emph{ddi} (data-dependence internal) links an input operand to an output operand of the same instruction.
evidence: tikz/execvocab_v2_8pt.tex:30; sections/background.tex:11; STT_6.als:79-81,155-158 (rf in outs->ins, ddi in ~ins.outs); URGENT_TODO.md:10 (ddi decided); FIGURES.md #71A

anchor: E.g. the speculative program order (spo) relation must be a total order on instructions.
comment: Why the order is 'speculative' is never said, and pipeline.tex:20 calls it 'a total program order'; Background introduces po. pipeline.tex:83 and :99 also say the harness 'enforces speculative program order', which only makes sense once spo is defined as fetch order including the wrong path.
proposed: \emph{Speculative program order} (spo) is the order in which the processor fetches instructions, including those on a mispredicted path; unlike MCM program order (po), it can contain instructions that never commit.
evidence: documentation/simspect-master.md:68 ('spo: speculative program order ... SPO vs PO, because we are targeting an execution'); sections/background.tex:11; sections/pipeline.tex:20,83,99

anchor: A \emph{per-branch resolve-stall} delays a branch's resolution to slide the speculative window over the transmitter.
comment: Each stall has several names: per-branch resolve-stall / resolve delay / resolved-branch stall $s_R$; unresolved-branch stall $s_U$ / long stall / 5000-cycle resolve stall / resolution held; commit-stall / fnc-stall / fnc-commit-stall / fnc stall / commit stall. Name each once and reuse it in results.tex:147-150, Table II and the timing figure.
proposed: We use three timing knobs: the \emph{resolve delay} $s_R$ (cycles a correctly predicted branch waits before resolving), the \emph{unresolved hold} $s_U$ (cycles an unresolved branch or store is kept unresolved), and the \emph{commit stall} (cycles \texttt{fnc} is held at the ROB head).
evidence: sections/pipeline.tex:72,75,86,89,92,94; sections/results.tex:147-150; tikz/instrtable_v2_8pt.tex:52,58,73; tikz/checkerwindow_v4_8pt.tex:133; FIGURES.md glossary undefined list

anchor: a defense that prevents leakage by delaying 'tainted' transmitters.
comment: 'Taint' is used heavily (results, all bug figures) but is only glossed in Background as 'tainted, or secret, piece of state'; its relation to the protection set is never stated, and untaint is never defined. The quotes are also straight quotes.
proposed: a defense that marks the results of speculative loads \emph{tainted}, its run-time form of the protection set, and delays any transmitter whose leaked operand is tainted until the taint is cleared (\emph{untainted}) when the load reaches its visibility point~\cite{stt}.
evidence: yu-2019-stt.pdf Sec. 6.1 ('STT untaints the output of an access instruction once it becomes safe'); sections/background.tex:3; sections/results.tex:87-115
